## Packet wire

Constants, enums, flags and types: bit-packed structs exchanged between client and server with exactly the same protocol version.

A cell is ✅ when the language's packet leg passes on this branch: the examples generated and run against the shared wire vectors the C++ reference writes (make test-<lang>), with the packet-text (#519), packet-wide (#188) and packet-defaults (#396) gates and their negative controls.

## Fixed Tables

Fixed tables provide versioning such that a new reader can always read an old writer. They are good for messages between the game server and a backend, or the backend and the website where the reader and writer have different versions of the protocol.

This work is on main: sprint/schema-vt-core landed on main, and the Go core (sprint/schema-go) lands through dev (2026-10-21). Cells show ✅ verified complete or ❌ not yet verified complete: a cell is ✅ only when every task under it is done with its acceptance recorded, by the landed cards, in docs/roadmap-evidence/. Built, partial and unstarted states stay in the source data; the [feature survey](docs/FIXED-TABLES-SURVEY.md) records the full scope.

## Variable tables

Progress checkpoint: 2026-11-02. Completed work is landing incrementally in main through PR #2660 and PR #2666. This roadmap records the current implementation and known gaps; unfinished work no longer holds completed changes on branches. The original nine languages remain the priority.

Registration now covers all 11 active constructs in C#, Go, Rust, Java, JavaScript, Dart and Elixir; C registers 10/11, with unbounded text remaining. The current C++ public registry lists 5/11; its additional landed implementation still needs registry and acceptance reconciliation. These counts describe compiler declarations, not percentages of full Schema completion.

Landed: required-field, forms, integrity and text-list implementation across the ports; stronger ordinary-positive-unit coverage; populated feature witnesses; pointer-target and root-closure regressions; neutral repeated-key widening and message-integrity repairs; Rust nested-reader refusal repair; JavaScript helper emission and blob accounting; Dart string identity and retained-record accounting; Elixir measurement, pointer and root-closure repairs. Shared failing inputs stay in the corpus.

C/C++/Go update: Go repeated-map-key widening is repaired across region and builder readers, with the exact shared failing input. Remaining: C unbounded text and text-form/report coverage, C map roadmap reconciliation, C++ active-construct registration, and full nightly acceptance.

C# update: unbounded-text and map-key copying through NativeCopyField/CopyRegion is repaired, with 5000-byte ownership regression coverage and a full native table suite passing. Repeated-map-key widening is also repaired in managed and native scans, with four-reader regression coverage and the shared failing input. Remaining: full-roster builder/retaining driver alignment and full nightly acceptance.

Remaining Rust: the final full nightly rerun after the nested-reader and neutral-reference fixes was stopped before completion. Its implementation and bounded regression repairs have landed; full acceptance is still open.

Java update: repeated-map-key widening and required-blob shared report accounting are repaired, including repeated-load, report-reset and null-report regression coverage. Caller-built equal strings and retained shared-wire refusal are covered. Complete retaining/fuzzer acceptance remains open. JavaScript update: package-derived UnitRegistry name collisions are repaired, with emitted-name regression and packet-only scope control. Final full-roster acceptance remains open.

Dart update: repeated-map-key widening is repaired with plain/retaining tests and the exact shared failing input. Cursor and node-table length checks now validate remaining extent before addition; the three original overflow inputs are in the shared corpus and pass native JIT/AOT regression tests. Remaining: cook-open/write proof and nightly builder/retirement controls. Elixir update: truncated payload framing is repaired for direct children and retained array elements, with 106-case native coverage. Enum collection references outside the ID table now report malformed, with 21-case native coverage and an exact shared regression input. Unknown-enum retention accounting is still under repair; full nightly acceptance remains open. Their complete retaining/fuzzer acceptance remains open.

Known defects reopen the affected cells below. Historical passing receipts remain evidence for their original scope, not proof of the expanded current gate. Current full-roster nightly acceptance remains incomplete across the nine, so the wire-fuzzer row is open. Uncommitted followups are preserved outside this snapshot; no all-nine completion or release claim is made.

Schema is built by Glenn Fiedler, together with AI collaborators that do much of the building, testing and porting. Glenn owns every design decision. Every month a [public ledger](https://github.com/mas-bandwidth/patreon#public-ledgers) shows where the AI collaborator's tokens went, by repository, and what they bought.
